title: Resolution of a Vector
notes:
Definition

The process of splitting a vector into its components is called resolution of a vector.

Examples

  • Ax = Acosθ, Ay = Asinθ (Case I)
  • Ax = Asinθ, Ay = Acosθ (Case II)
examples:
**Q1: Define resolution of a vector.**

**Answer:** The process of splitting a vector into its components.

**Q2: In Case I, what is Ax equal to?**

**Answer:** Ax = Acosθ.

**Q3: In Case I, what is Ay equal to?**

**Answer:** Ay = Asinθ.

**Q4: In Case II, what is Ax equal to?**

**Answer:** Ax = Asinθ.

**Q5: In Case II, what is Ay equal to?**

**Answer:** Ay = Acosθ.

**Q6: If A = 10N and θ = 30° (Case I), find Ax.**

**Answer:** Ax = 10cos30° ≈ 8.66N.

**Q7: If A = 10N and θ = 30° (Case I), find Ay.**

**Answer:** Ay = 10sin30° = 5N.

**Q8: Why is resolving a vector into components useful?**

**Answer:** It simplifies vector addition/analysis by allowing algebraic addition of components along fixed axes.

**Q9: What is the relationship between A, Ax, and Ay?**

**Answer:** A² = Ax² + Ay² (Pythagorean relation).

**Q10: If Ax = 3 and Ay = 4, find |A|.**

**Answer:** |A| = √(9+16) = 5.

**Q11: What angle formula relates θ, Ax, and Ay in Case I?**

**Answer:** tanθ = Ay/Ax.

**Q12: In Case I, what trigonometric ratio gives cosθ?**

**Answer:** cosθ = Ax/A (adjacent/hypotenuse).

**Q13: In Case I, what trigonometric ratio gives sinθ?**

**Answer:** sinθ = Ay/A (opposite/hypotenuse).

**Q14: Why does resolving into components help in adding multiple vectors?**

**Answer:** Because component-wise (x and y) addition is simple algebraic addition, unlike direct vector addition of the full vectors.

**Q15: If A = 20N at 60° above x-axis, find its x-component.**

**Answer:** Ax = 20cos60° = 10N.

**Q16: If A = 20N at 60° above x-axis, find its y-component.**

**Answer:** Ay = 20sin60° ≈ 17.32N.

**Q17: What is the physical meaning of the x-component of a vector?**

**Answer:** The projection/effect of the vector along the x-axis.

**Q18: What is the physical meaning of the y-component of a vector?**

**Answer:** The projection/effect of the vector along the y-axis.

**Q19: If a vector lies entirely along the x-axis, what is its y-component?**

**Answer:** Zero.

**Q20: If a vector lies entirely along the y-axis, what is its x-component?**

**Answer:** Zero.

**Q21: Give a real-world application of vector resolution.**

**Answer:** Resolving the weight of an object on an inclined plane into components parallel and perpendicular to the plane.

**Q22: If Ax = Acosθ and θ = 90°, what is Ax?**

**Answer:** 0, since cos90° = 0.

**Q23: If Ay = Asinθ and θ = 90°, what is Ay?**

**Answer:** A, since sin90° = 1 (the full magnitude lies along y).

**Q24: How would you resolve a force of 50N acting at 45° into its two rectangular components?**

**Answer:** Fx = 50cos45° ≈ 35.36N, Fy = 50sin45° ≈ 35.36N.

**Q25: Why are Case I and Case II different in the notes?**

**Answer:** They correspond to different reference angle placements (angle measured from x-axis vs from y-axis), swapping which component uses sine vs cosine.

**Q26: What geometric shape is used (ΔOPQ) to derive the resolution formulas?**

**Answer:** A right-angled triangle formed by the vector and its two perpendicular components.
keyPoints: - **Definition:** The process of splitting a vector into its components is called resolution of a vector.
summary: The process of splitting a vector into its components is called resolution of a vector. Key examples include Ax = Acosθ, Ay = Asinθ (Case I); Ax = Asinθ, Ay = Acosθ (Case II). Includes 26 short-answer practice questions.
